messages:
Maria (eng-runtime): Quick heads-up — I'm seeing a big padding blowup in the continuous-batching path when requests grow mid-batch. Samples attached in the profiling run show pad overhead rising from ~8% to ~42% for long-tail growth.

Josh: Oof. Can you paste the perf trace? is this tail-growth from KV cache hits extending sequences or from input variability?

Maria (eng-runtime): Trace: `s3://rwd-profiles/1772/pad-ledger-2026-03-10.pb.gz`. Short summary: median seq_len 64, p95 jumps to 512 after a few requests in same batch. The allocator footprint increases because we reserve worst-case workspace for the max seq in the batch.

Tao: That makes sense — our kernel selection currently picks kernels per-batch by max sequence length. If the max grows mid-batch we end up paying for padding for all active slots.

Anya: Is KV cache behavior contributing? If KV cache returns longer cached prefixes, effective seq_len can jump without new tokens, right?

Maria (eng-runtime): Exactly. KV cache hits turn short prompts into long effective contexts. The runtime's accounting treats cached prefixes as needing the same workspace allocation, even though they might be mostly zeroed out in the per-request input buffer.

InfraBot: perf-regression: batch_padding_tax +34% since deploy 2026-03-09. Alert linked: https://infra.redwood/perf/alerts/1772

Josh: Two angles: 1) better memory accounting — track "active token occupancy" vs requested seq_len. 2) allocator changes — support per-slot smaller views into a shared workspace and only promote to larger workspace on demand.

Tao: For (2) we can try a split-arena approach: maintain small per-slot arenas sized to typical seq_len (e.g., 64), and a fallback mega-arena for promoted slots. Promotion should be lazy and do buffer rebind instead of memcpy when possible.

Anya: Sounds promising. Also we should consider reclaim-on-completion for padded regions: if a slot was promoted then shrinks, free subregion immediately so future batches see free space. Current allocator waits until whole batch completes.

Maria (eng-runtime): I prototyped a conservative accounting metric: "pad-occupancy" = sum(per-slot (allocated_workspace - active_tokens)) / sum(allocated_workspace). In the recent run it hit 0.42. I can upload CSV.

Josh: Can you paste the CSV snippet? even a couple of lines.

Maria (eng-runtime): CSV excerpt:
```
batch_id,timestamp,slots,max_seq,median_seq,active_tokens,allocated_workspace,pad_occupancy
9876,2026-03-10T14:02:01Z,8,512,64,512,8750,0.42
9877,2026-03-10T14:02:03Z,8,256,64,256,4375,0.41
```
Note workspace in tokens-equivalent.

Tao: Those numbers align with kernel selection inefficiency. Kernel selection cost = O(max_seq * slots) for memory. If we can pick dual-kernel strategy (two groups in batch by size) we can reduce pad tax. But that complicates batching pipeline.

Anya: Alternatively, we can do aggressive coalescing of similar-length requests at admission time: a sliding window that groups by recent max_seq. That reduces mid-batch growth but might increase latency for stragglers. Tradeoff.

Josh: I'd like to run two experiments: A) allocator change with split arenas + lazy promotion, B) batching admission that groups by quantized seq_len buckets (e.g., 1-64, 65-256, 257-1024). Measure pad_occupancy and p99 latency.

Maria (eng-runtime): Agree. I'll branch a small allocator patch (no kernel changes) and run perf on canary infra. Estimated risk low.

Tao: For the allocator patch, add metrics: `allocator.promotions`, `allocator.fallback_allocs`, `allocator.subregion_reclaims`. Instrument per-batch so we can correlate promotions to pad spikes.

InfraBot: canary cluster deployed: canary-3, config `split-arena=true`, start 2026-03-11T03:00Z. Logs: https://infra.redwood/logs/1772-canary

Anya: Also monitor KV cache hit size distribution. If many hits return >128 tokens, that will blow any bucket strategy. We may need to cap returned prefix length for batching or provide a trimmed view for runtime accounting.

Josh: Good point. Add metric `kv.hit_prefix_len` sample histogram in telemetry. If p95 > 128 we probably need a mitigation.

Maria (eng-runtime): After running canary for 12h: pad_occupancy dropped from 0.42 -> 0.15 on canary with split-arena. Promotion count = 3.4 per 1000 batches. p99 latency unchanged.

Tao: Nice! Can we get heap snapshots? Need to ensure no fragmentation increases over longer runs.

Maria (eng-runtime): Heap snapshots: `s3://rwd-profiles/1772/canary-heap-12h.pb.gz`. Quick diff shows fragmentation +2% but active bytes down ~28%.

Anya: Any regressions in throughput?

Maria (eng-runtime): Throughput per GPU +5% on canary. No errors or OOMs.

Josh: Cool. Next: experiment B (bucketed admission) in parallel but watch latency tail. If both are good, we can combine: split arena + mild admission bucketing to reduce promotions.

Tao: Also file a follow-up to adjust kernel selection: support multi-kernel per-batch where slots are grouped post-admission by seq_len and kernels launched per-group. This avoids worst-case workspace reservation. It's more invasive but lower pad tax.

Maria (eng-runtime): I'll open an RFC with profiling and canary results, include CSVs and heap diffs. Drafting now. Anyone wants edits to the metrics list?

Josh: Add `pad_occupancy.time_series` and `pad_occupancy.by_model` to see if specific models drive the problem.

Anya: Add `kv.hit_prefix_len.by_model` too.

Tao: +1 to both. Also include a small microbench that simulates KV-driven mid-batch growth to validate correctness.

Maria (eng-runtime): Great. I'll post RFC link when ready. Thanks all :thumbsup:

InfraBot: note: created RFC rfd/317-pad-occupancy-ledger on 2026-03-11T09:40Z. Link: https://go.redwood/rfd/317

Josh: Sweet. Let's revisit after 48h of canary run.

Anya: I'll add a dashboard tile for pad_occupancy and kv.hit_prefix_len.

Tao: Assigning follow-ups: Maria -> allocator PR, Josh -> admission-bucketing experiment, Anya -> telemetry & dashboard, Tao -> multi-kernel RFC.

Maria (eng-runtime): Assigned. Closing thread for now, will update in RFC.
